title: Vessel wall thickness tracks radius in large arteries but falls off in small ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Vessel wall thickness tracks radius in large arteries but falls off in small ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Under constant pressure the wall thickness of a blood-vessel should vary as its radius (P = T/R); because pressure falls with friction from large to small arteries, wall thickness is proportional to vessel size in larger vessels but becomes disproportionately thin in small arteries and capillaries.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: P = T/R; at constant P, wall thickness t \propto R

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: and accordingly we find that while, for a time, the cross-sections of the larger and smaller vessels are symmetrical figures, with the wall-thickness proportional to the size of the tube, this proportion is gradually lost, and the walls of the small arteries, and still more of the capillaries, become exceedingly thin, and more so than in strict proportion to the narrowing of the tube.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Blood-vessel walls”. Scope: arteries and capillaries of vertebrates

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: P = T/R; at constant P, wall thickness t \propto R

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The scaling relation and deviation are explicit. Relevant open measurements exist, but joining vessel-scale anatomy to local pressure across the complete arterial-capillary range requires heterogeneous sources.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure lumen radius, wall thickness and pressure along arterial trees and fit the predicted large-vessel proportionality and small-vessel downward deviation. Models with and without pressure decline can be compared.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Capillary wall thickness requires histology or microscopy.

Geometry and local pressure are generally not measured in the same subjects.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decision rule is the Laplace scaling Thompson states: thickness tracks radius while pressure is roughly constant, then falls off as pressure drops. Open whole-body anatomy shows the large-vessel half of that pattern in humans. Capillaries and non-human vertebrates are poorly represented in downloadable volumes, so a full test across the stated scope still needs a histological compilation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Along arterial trees, regress wall thickness on lumen radius separately for large arteries and for small arteries and capillaries. Support would be a near-proportional relation in the large vessels and a clear drop in thickness-to-radius in the small ones; a single proportion across the whole size range, or walls that stay thick in capillaries, would refute the stated pattern.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Visible Human resolution does not reach capillary walls, and the claim's small-vessel limb depends on histology scattered through papers.

Elastic and muscular arteries differ in wall composition, so a single Laplace proportion is confounded by vessel class.
